_about: What a receiver must answer. Each case starts from fixture.json's record and changes one thing: `set` replaces a value at a dotted path (a list index is a number), `repeat_commits` repeats the first commit until there are that many, `pad` adds an unknown key holding that many characters. `token` is `valid` (the receiver's test token), `unknown`, or `none`. Only the status is matched: a receiver words its own refusals.

cases.name: a valid record
cases.why: the record the contract describes is stored

cases.name: a key the receiver does not read
cases.why: unknown keys are dropped, never refused — a sender adding one breaks nobody

cases.name: a schema version the receiver does not read
cases.why: a receiver refuses a shape it does not know rather than storing half of it

cases.name: a commit hash that is not one
cases.why: every field is validated, and the body is refused whole

cases.name: more commits than one request may carry
cases.why: a longer range is sent in parts of at most 500

cases.name: a body larger than a receiver reads
cases.why: the size limit is checked before anything is parsed

cases.name: no token
cases.why: a record is stored only for the app whose token sent it

cases.name: an unknown token
cases.why: a revoked or invented token stores nothing
